subject: Re: [AMBER] partial charge calculation (RESP) using gaussian09/antechamber (ambertools17) on a symmetrical molecule

messages.author: BLUNTZER Marie
messages.body:
________________________________
From: BLUNTZER Marie
Sent: 08 October 2020 11:50
To: AMBER Mailing List <amber.ambermd.org>
Subject: partial charge calculation (RESP) using gaussian09/antechamber (ambertools17) on a symmetrical molecule
good morning
I am computing the MEP/ESP using gaussian09 of 100 conformers (generated using RDkit) of a symmetrical molecule using the HF/6-31* basis set.
Then I am using antechamber to compute the RESP
using the command
antechamber -i  %s.log -fi gout -o %s.mol2 -fo mol2 -c resp -at amber   -eq 2  -pf   -dr n at
which as I understand it, calls a certain number of background scripts and notably the resp command
On my system it picked up the symmetry for 81 conformers returning me identical partial charges for equivalent atoms but for 19 conformers the symmetry was not picked up when building the  ANTECHAMBER_RESP1.IN and ANTECHAMBER_RESP2.IN files and  equivalent atoms did not return identical charges.
I tweaked and decomposed the antechamber command replacing the resp input  by the ones of a conformers that had picked up the symmetry and that gave me the expected output, but that is a bit troublesome ...
Is that a bug? Has it been fixed in more recent versions of antechamber ?
I have attached the conformer 1 (conformer where antechamber picked up the symmetry) and the conformer 13 where the symmetry was not picked up
Best
Marie

messages.author: James Kress
messages.body:
Using the coordinates you posted, it would appear that molecules 1 and 13
are both of point group C1 (determined using Chemcraft).  Were you expecting
something different?
Why are you using symmetry with G9?  The possible reduction in compute time
is minimal, especially when the molecules are both point group C1.

messages.author: BLUNTZER Marie
messages.body:
Thank you for your answer
They are both the same molecule actually, just different conformers.
This molecule is indeed a C1 because the alkyl group is Z (cis) and the two chiral Carbons are S, so I guess you are right about the symmetry in g09 it does not do much in that case.
Howerer if the chiral centers are taken out, the molecule is 'symmetrical' and antechamber manage to detect that symmetry for one conformer assigning identical charges in the RESP calculation for equivalent atoms for one conformer but not the other conformer.
Whether the charges should be identical or not (that is actually a reasonable question), I am just surprised that antechamber does not treat the symmetry in a similar manner for 2 conformers of the same molecule.
Best
Marie
